scope: Theorem G.1 (Pinning obstruction) of the manuscript “Uniform Cartier sections for Fano type contractions” (preprints/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026/Uniform-Cartier-sections-for-Fano-type-contractions-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 066 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8d97ba60373419ba), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 80-81. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an integer n > 0 and ϵ > 0. There is no sequence of the following data satisfying all the conditions below. For each index i, let xi ∈ Si be an n-dimensional complex klt germ with an action of a finite cyclic group Γi fixing xi, such that 80 the quotient map is quasi-étale and Si/Γi is ϵ-lc. Suppose KSi has a nowhere-vanishing local eigen-generator ωi, and let hi be a nonzero regular eigenfunction with the same character χi as ωi. The character need not be faithful. Assume that (Si, div(hi)) is lc and admits a centred quasi-monomial valuation Ti with ASi (Ti) = Ti(hi) = 1. The excluded additional condition is: for every fixed integer m > 0, there is an index i(m) such that, for all i ≥ i(m) and every regular semi-invariant s of character χm i , Ti(s) ≥ m. (G.1)
